Subject: Redwood RFP — commercial clarifications (ZenHealth)

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the RFP response — the commercial appendix raised a few follow-up questions from our procurement and finance teams. We condensed them into the attached spreadsheet but wanted to surface the highest-priority clarifications so your pricing team can respond in the RFP timeline.

1) Commit structure: Do you support annual and monthly committed token bands? For annual commits, what is the default monthly invoicing cadence and true-up behavior at quarter and year end?

2) Excess / surge rates: Please provide the proposed overage rate schedule when usage exceeds committed bands. Is there a hard cap or stepped waterfall?

3) Protection mechanism: We are evaluating a short-term "shelter" or smoothing layer to protect against temporary spikes. Can you propose a billing-first approach (credits / escrow / amortized credits) you have used for other large customers?

4) Invoice examples: Please provide two illustrative monthly invoices (one within commit, one with a 40% spike). Show how credits and overages apply.

5) Discounts & renewal: How do volume discounts tier with multi-year commitments and do you offer rollback protection if usage drops materially?

6) Contractual SLO credits: If we hit latency/availability credits tied to commit bands, how are those applied to invoices?

We'd like a short commercial appendix PDF and any sample invoice workpapers back by EOD Monday (2026-08-31). Attached is the procurement worksheet we referenced.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alicia

Sean / Priyom — high level proposal attached and pasted below. Kept two clean options + a glide path sample invoice.

Option A — Fixed Annual Commit (preferred for predictability)
- Annual commit (tokens): 120M tokens/year (10M/month baseline).
- Price: $0.0006/token at commit band.
- Overages: Tiered waterfall: 0–20% over: +35% to base rate; 20–100%: +70%; >100%: +150% (applied per-month on overage volume).
- True-up: Quarterly true-up with final year-end reconciliation; unused commit does not roll unless agreed.
- SLA crediting: applied as invoice-level credit pro rata to the month in which SLO breach occurred.

Option B — Tier Shelter (new suggestion)
- Annual commit same as A, with a two-month Tier Shelter equal to 1.5x monthly baseline tokens (applies only to 2 non-consecutive months per year).
- Mechanic: Shelter funded by 1% of committed spend deposited to a restricted credit pool (escrow on invoice 1). Credits consumed during shelter months reduce overage billing; remaining escrow balance amortized back as a monthly credit over remaining months if unused.
- Overages outside shelter: stepped waterfall above.

Corridor Example — soft smoothing
- Rolling 3-month corridor: if month N > 130% of 3-month rolling avg, apply amortized credit equal to (excess - 130%) spread evenly over next 3 months, capped at 50% of next month's billed overage.

Sample invoice (Month with 40% spike over baseline) — attached spreadsheet shows line items: committed charge, used tokens, overage calculation by tier, shelter credit applied, escrow deposit, final amount due.

Numbers are illustrative; if procurement wants a different shelter size (e.g., 2 months at 2x baseline) we can run sensitivity. I attached a scenario workbook.

-Marissa
Head of Enterprise Pricing
Redwood Inference

Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Attached is a concise commercial appendix + scenario workbook that shows two options (A, B) and a corridor alternative you can present to finance. Highlights below; the PDF includes the illustrative invoices you requested.

Executive summary
- Option A (Predictable): Annual commit (120M tokens) with stepped overage waterfall. Best for predictable budgeting.
- Option B (Tier Shelter): Same commit, escrow-funded 2-month shelter for transient spikes. Shelter reduces overage volatility and preserves long-term economics.
- Corridor (Smoothing): Rolling 3-month amortization option for soft spikes without up-front escrow.

Key mechanics (how shelter works)
- Initial escrow: 1% of committed annual spend invoiced in month 1 and held as a restricted credit balance.
- Consumption: Shelter covers X tokens during declared shelter months; consumed credits reduce overage computation for that month.
- Unused escrow: amortized as a monthly credit across remaining months.

Attached deliverables
- Redwood_Appendix_Proposal_V2.pdf — short commercial appendix with narrative + sample invoices.
- Redwood_Commercial_Model_Scenarios.xlsx — monthly invoice workpapers (two scenarios: baseline and 40% spike).

Links & next steps
- HubSpot record: HS-1234567 (I will attach final PDF there).
- If ZenHealth likes Option B we can add a one-page contract amendment describing escrow handling and reporting cadence.

If helpful, we can jump on a 30-minute call this week to walk through invoice mechanics — Marissa and I are available tomorrow 10–12 PT or Wednesday afternoon.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
